description: Sourced cybersecurity and AI vendor intelligence for banks

items.title: Dataset version 2026-11-23
items.content_text: 40 new vendors, 49 new products, 0 score changes, 0 vendor status changes, 240 events recorded.

items.title: launch: Concentric AI announces an endpoint agent for Semantic DLP
items.content_text: Concentric AI announced the Semantic DLP Agent, extending its controls from the browser to desktop AI applications, coding agents and locally run models, with analysis of whether a prompt fits the user's role.

items.title: launch: GetReal Protect for Microsoft Teams listed in Microsoft Marketplace
items.content_text: GetReal Security said on 2026-11-19 that its Microsoft Teams integration is available in Microsoft Marketplace and that it is taking part in Microsoft's programme for certified third-party synthetic audio and video detection in Teams, with certification in progress.

items.title: vulnerability disclosure: GitGuardian patches self-hosted Embedded Cluster installs against nginx HTTP/2 flaws
items.content_text: GitGuardian announced in a customer notice dated 2026-11-19 that Embedded Cluster installations of its self-hosted edition on releases 2025.1.0 to 2026.11.0 were exposed to two nginx HTTP/2 vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, reachable on port 443, and that release 2026.11.1 turns HTTP/2 off in the bundled ingress. Helm and KOTS installations on an existing cluster and the hosted service were not listed as affected. The notice does not say whether the flaws were exploited.

items.title: launch: Immersive announces Immersive AI Security in early access
items.content_text: On 18 November 2026 the company announced a new product family, Immersive AI Security, with two products: AI Govern & Control, which monitors and controls how staff use AI tools in the browser, and AI Observe & Assess, an on-premises appliance that maps and tests internally built AI agents. Both link findings to training in Immersive One. They are in an early-access programme, with general availability planned for early 2027.

items.title: security incident: Infoblox investigates data exposure through a compromised third-party vendor
items.content_text: Reported by The Register on 2026-11-16 and by Cyber Daily on 2026-11-17: Infoblox said it was investigating unauthorised access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor. The Register, citing sources and an email from the chief executive, reported that the intruders used the vendor's access to Infoblox's SharePoint and that the data included personal and payroll details of employees and their dependants and saved configuration snapshots of some customers' NIOS deployments. A company spokesperson told both outlets there was no indication that Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. Infoblox did not say how many customers or employees were affected.

items.title: launch: PKI Spotlight adds monitoring of Utimaco u.trust general purpose HSMs
items.content_text: PKI Solutions announced monitoring of Utimaco u.trust GP HSMs in PKI Spotlight, including the state of each container HSM and events on configuration changes, collected without HSM login credentials. Utimaco lists PKI Solutions as a technology partner.

items.title: launch: Flashpoint announces an agentic AI offering for Ignite, due in early 2027
items.content_text: Flashpoint announced on 10 November 2026 an offering called Flashpoint Agentic AI: a hub in Ignite combining chat-driven investigations with agents for intelligence briefings, alert set-up, alert triage and drafting intelligence requirements. The company said it would be available in early 2027 as a separate offering from the AI features already included with product licences.

items.title: acquisition: Guardsquare announces acquisitions of Runway and Bugfender
items.content_text: Guardsquare announced that it had acquired Runway, a mobile release management platform, and Bugfender, a remote logging and crash-reporting provider, adding release management and crash analytics to its mobile security products. Terms were not disclosed.

items.title: partnership: OneSpan FIDO technology selected for Japan's TSUBASA Alliance shared authentication
items.content_text: OneSpan announced that its FIDO authentication technology was selected for an initiative in which participating banks of Japan's TSUBASA Alliance, a ten-member grouping of regional banks, will set up shared authentication infrastructure for their mobile personal banking apps. The participating banks were not named and no launch date was given.

items.title: acquisition: Doppel acquires PropRise and adds its founders to its engineering team
items.content_text: Doppel announced on 4 November 2026 that it had acquired PropRise, a Y Combinator-backed company founded in 2023, and that its two founders would join Doppel's engineering organisation. Pulse 2.0 reported the deal on 7 November 2026. No price was given.

items.title: launch: Absolute Secure Endpoint adds Linux support
items.content_text: Absolute Security announced that the Secure Endpoint agent supports Ubuntu and Red Hat Enterprise Linux workstations, with inventory and device freeze available at once and patching and automation in selected editions. The release also announced self-hosted Secure Access deployments for US federal and state organisations.

items.title: partnership: Black Kite announces integration with CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM
items.content_text: Black Kite announced an integration that delivers its third-party vendor risk intelligence into CrowdStrike Falcon Next-Gen SIEM for use in security operations workflows.

items.title: leadership change: Fastly's president, go to market, Scott Lovett to retire in 2027
items.content_text: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K filed on 4 November 2026 that Scott Lovett notified the company on 30 October 2026 of his planned retirement as president, go to market, on a date to be set during 2027. He stays in the role while a new chief revenue officer is recruited and will then act as a senior adviser until at least 30 June 2027.

items.title: launch: AppViewX offers Quantum Trust Hub as a standalone product and adds Qualys discovery
items.content_text: AppViewX announced that Quantum Trust Hub is available as a standalone solution, with discovery from existing Qualys scan data alongside Tenable, upload of third-party bills of materials, business-context risk ranking and ServiceNow remediation tickets.

items.title: launch: Fable Security makes AI voice-phishing simulations generally available
items.content_text: Fable Security announced on 29 October 2026 the general availability of voice-phishing simulations: AI voice calls to employees and shared lines using pretexts such as password and MFA resets, vendor payment changes and executive impersonation, with coaching after the call and results fed into each person's risk profile. The pricing page lists it as an add-on sold separately.

items.title: launch: ReversingLabs launches Spectra Assure Catalog for approved software downloads
items.content_text: ReversingLabs announced on 2026-10-28 Spectra Assure Catalog, which publishes for internal download only software packages that pass the customer's policy after binary analysis. The vendor says it is available to existing Spectra Assure customers and switched on by default.

items.title: vulnerability disclosure: Veeam discloses a critical authorisation bypass fixed in Backup & Replication 13.1.2
items.content_text: Disclosed by Veeam on 2026-10-27 in knowledge base article KB4948: CVE-2026-108142, rated critical (CVSS v4.0 9.1), allowed an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authorisation on the CDP Coordinator Service in version 13.0 and 13.1 builds; two medium-severity path traversal flaws were fixed in the same builds, 13.1.2 and 13.0.3. Veeam said the flaws were reported through its HackerOne programme; version 12 is not affected. None appears in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue version read on 2026-11-23.

items.title: certification: Aikido says its government edition is FedRAMP Moderate authorised through Knox Systems
items.content_text: Aikido's changelog of 2026-10-22 announced FedRAMP Moderate status. Its FedRAMP page says the separate Aikido for Government edition has been authorised since October 2026 inside Knox Systems' FedRAMP boundary on AWS GovCloud. The FedRAMP Marketplace data file read on 2026-11-23 lists Knox Systems as FedRAMP Authorized at Moderate and does not name Aikido.

items.title: launch: Bolster AI introduces Threat Graph for linking related findings into campaigns
items.content_text: In a blog post dated 20 October 2026, Bolster AI introduced Threat Graph, a view inside Signals that connects related URLs, domains, hosting providers, phone numbers, emails and social accounts so a campaign can be investigated together. A knowledge-base article updated the same day documents it.

items.title: launch: Transmit Security unveils Agentic Trust for detecting and governing AI agents
items.content_text: Alongside its change of chief executive, the vendor announced Agentic Trust for financial institutions and merchants: detection of AI-agent traffic in online channels, classification of the agent and its intent, and controls to allow, limit, hold for customer approval or stop an agent's actions. The release gives no general-availability date or price.

items.title: leadership change: Transmit Security names Matt Thompson chief executive; co-founder Mickey Boodaei becomes chairman
items.content_text: Transmit Security named Matt Thompson, previously president and chief commercial officer of Socure, as chief executive. BankInfoSecurity and CTech reported that co-founder Mickey Boodaei, chief executive since the company's founding in 2014, becomes chairman and stays involved in product strategy.

items.title: partnership: Memcyco appoints IBI Group as reseller in India
items.content_text: Memcyco and Mumbai-based security firm IBI Group announced a partnership under which IBI Group will resell and co-market Memcyco's services in India, starting with banking and financial services, fintech, e-commerce and critical infrastructure.

items.title: acquisition: Absolute Security acquires FirmGuard from Phoenix Technologies
items.content_text: Absolute Security announced the acquisition of FirmGuard, a firmware security and management service for UEFI BIOS, from Phoenix Technologies for an undisclosed price, to add firmware integrity checking, posture management and patching to its platform.

items.title: leadership change: Censys appoints Jeff Hackett as chief financial officer
items.content_text: Censys's newsroom lists a release dated 6 October 2026 announcing Jeff Hackett as chief financial officer; he appears in that role on the leadership page.

items.title: merger: NetSPI and Synack complete their merger
items.content_text: Synack states that the merger with NetSPI was completed on 2026-10-05; NetSPI's page says it closed in October 2026 after regulatory approvals. Both say each company continues to deliver its own platform, services and agreements for now, that no combined product or contract exists yet, and that Synack's FedRAMP Moderate authorisation is unchanged and does not extend to NetSPI products.

items.title: launch: PKI Spotlight adds Intune Cloud PKI visibility and wider EJBCA monitoring
items.content_text: The third-quarter 2026 release added visibility of Microsoft Cloud PKI certificate authorities connected through Intune, extended EJBCA data into certificates, revocation lists, topology and best-practice alerts, introduced common connection and service status views, and added a cryptography governance area to the built-in maturity self-assessment.

items.title: launch: First release of Spectra Resolve, an AI-assisted dependency remediation tool
items.content_text: The Spectra Assure documentation changelog records the first release of Spectra Resolve on 2026-10-01. The documentation describes it as a desktop application in which an AI coding agent checks whether flagged dependencies are reachable and proposes an upgrade, a code fix or a risk acceptance for a person to approve.

items.title: launch: Memcyco releases PoSA v1.11 with Attack Overview and a Risk API
items.content_text: Memcyco released version 1.11 of PoSA, adding earlier identification of attacker devices, an Attack Overview that links events affecting the same user, and a Risk API that returns user and device risk scores with their underlying signals before access is granted. SecurityBrief reported the release on 13 October 2026.

items.title: launch: Acalvio launches ShadowPlex AI Agent in the Gemini Enterprise agent marketplace
items.content_text: Acalvio announced on 29 September 2026 an AI agent, listed in the Gemini Enterprise agent marketplace and working with Google Cloud Gemini Enterprise, that turns a security objective written in plain language into a deception playbook for deployment through the ShadowPlex platform.

items.title: launch: Cribl launches Cribl Detect, a SIEM that includes detection posture management
items.content_text: Cribl announced Cribl Detect on 29 September 2026 and said it was available to Cribl.Cloud customers. The release lists detection posture management, which maps existing detections to MITRE ATT&CK and shows coverage gaps, broken or noisy rules and missing telemetry, alongside in-stream detections, federated investigation and AI-assisted triage. TechTarget reported that the product combines technology from the CardinalOps and Radiant Security deals and is not yet supported on premises or in self-managed environments. Cribl's documentation labels every Cribl Detect page as Preview and says the feature is not recommended for production environments.

items.title: funding: MUFG Innovation Partners invests in Doppel
items.content_text: Doppel announced on 24 September 2026 that MUFG Innovation Partners, the corporate venture arm of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group, had become a strategic investor. The investor's own notice, dated 25 September 2026, says the investment was made through its No. 3 investment partnership. Neither gave an amount.

items.title: launch: Fable Security launches Briefing Agent to turn threat reports and policies into employee briefings
items.content_text: Enterprise Security Tech reported on 17 September 2026 that Fable Security had launched Briefing Agent, an AI tool that drafts targeted security briefings from emerging threats and company policies. An administrator must approve the script, audience and delivery channel before a briefing is sent, and the tool keeps source material, prompts and revision history. It was made available to existing customers within their subscriptions.

items.title: partnership: PKI Solutions appoints Unsung as UK reseller and services partner
items.content_text: PKI Solutions announced that Unsung, a UK consultancy specialising in PKI, will resell PKI Spotlight in the UK and provide deployment, integration, remediation and operations services.

items.title: leadership change: Concentric AI appoints a chief revenue officer
items.content_text: Concentric AI announced the appointment of Gary Olson as chief revenue officer and Will Saso as vice-president of sales for the Americas.

items.title: certification: RegScale announces CMMC Level 2 certification
items.content_text: RegScale's newsroom carries a release, published on a wire service on 2 September 2026, announcing that the company achieved CMMC Level 2 certification. Its Security & Trust page says the certification was achieved in August 2026 with all 110 NIST SP 800-171 requirements met and that the assessor was A-LIGN. The date recorded is the date of the release.

items.title: merger: NetSPI and Synack announce an agreement to merge
items.content_text: NetSPI and Synack announced a definitive agreement to merge, stating combined revenue of more than US$200M. BankInfoSecurity reported on 2026-09-03 that the combined firm would be led by NetSPI and majority owned by KKR, NetSPI's majority owner since 2022, with about 800 staff. IT Brief reported an expected close in October. Deal terms were not published.

items.title: certification: Aikido announces ISO/IEC 42001 certification for its AI features
items.content_text: Aikido said on 2026-08-26 that it had been certified to ISO/IEC 42001:2023, with a scope covering the AI-enabled features of its platform, including AutoFix, AutoTriage, AI pentesting and code review. The post does not name the certification body or the certificate date; the event is dated to the announcement.

items.title: leadership change: Rubrik appoints Rakefet Russak-Aminoach to its board
items.content_text: Rubrik's Form 8-K states that, effective 26 August 2026, the board increased from eight to nine directors and appointed Rakefet Russak-Aminoach as a Class I director with a term expiring at the 2028 annual meeting.

items.title: launch: ExtraHop announces a 400 Gbps sensor for RevealX
items.content_text: On 25 August 2026 ExtraHop announced a sensor for RevealX that it says analyses data-centre traffic at 400 Gbps at line rate, with general availability expected in the fourth quarter of 2026. The throughput figure is the company's own; no independent measurement was found.

items.title: leadership change: Netcraft appoints Darren Lee to its board
items.content_text: On 25 August 2026 Netcraft announced that Darren Lee, formerly a senior executive at Proofpoint, had joined its board. Companies House records his appointment as a director of NC Topco Limited on 12 August 2026.

items.title: leadership change: Co-founder Orion Hindawi returns as Tanium chief executive
items.content_text: Tanium announced that co-founder Orion Hindawi, chief executive from 2016 to 2023, returned to the role with immediate effect, replacing Dan Streetman, who had been appointed in February 2023 and left the board. Co-founder David Hindawi returned as chairman.

items.title: acquisition: Cribl buys Radiant Security's AI security-operations technology assets
items.content_text: Cribl announced on 19 August 2026 that it had bought technology assets, including intellectual property for automated alert triage and investigation, from Radiant Security. It described this as its second security technology acquisition of the year after CardinalOps. Terms were not disclosed. The release describes a purchase of assets, not of the company.

items.title: funding: Fastly increases its revolving credit facility from US$60 million to US$100 million
items.content_text: Fastly reported in a Form 8-K that on 17 August 2026 it amended its credit agreement with Silicon Valley Bank, a division of First-Citizens Bank, raising the senior secured revolving facility from US$60 million to US$100 million, extending its scheduled maturity to 17 August 2029 subject to conditions tied to the 2028 convertible notes, and lowering the interest margin by 0.25%. The quarterly report for September 2026 says nothing was drawn on the facility.

items.title: vulnerability disclosure: Absolute publishes fixes in Secure Access 14.57
items.content_text: Absolute disclosed in its vulnerability archive on 2026-08-12 that Secure Access 14.57 fixed flaws that could allow denial of service by an attacker who controlled an authentication session or sat between client and server. The entry read lists no CVE identifiers and does not state that the flaws were exploited.

items.title: litigation: Court lets part of the securities class action against Fastly proceed
items.content_text: Reported by Fastly in its Form 10-Q filed on 4 November 2026: a putative securities class action filed on 24 May 2024 in the US District Court for the Northern District of California (case 4:24-cv-03170) names the company and certain officers, alleges violations of sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act on behalf of purchasers of Fastly securities between 15 November 2023 and 7 August 2024, and seeks unspecified damages. On 10 August 2026 the court granted in part and denied in part the defendants' motion to dismiss the second amended complaint, and the defendants filed an answer on 27 October 2026. The filing says six related stockholder derivative complaints have been filed and are stayed or subject to negotiated stays. No outcome has been decided.

items.title: acquisition: Infoblox completes acquisition of network observability company Kentik
items.content_text: Network World reported on 8 July 2026 that Infoblox had agreed to acquire Kentik, a network observability company, on undisclosed terms. Infoblox's release of 6 August 2026 says the acquisition has completed and that Kentik's capabilities will be integrated into its platform over time.

items.title: launch: Tidal Cyber adds a Model Context Protocol server for use with AI assistants
items.content_text: In a release dated 31 July 2026 and published on 3 August 2026, Tidal Cyber announced a Model Context Protocol server that lets approved AI assistants query the platform's threat profiles, coverage maps and recommendations in natural language, with authenticated, tenant-scoped access. It cites ChatGPT, Claude and Microsoft Copilot as examples of such assistants and says the capability is included in the platform.

items.title: launch: Acalvio launches Deception Guardrails for AI agents
items.content_text: Acalvio announced Deception Guardrails on 30 July 2026, a capability of the ShadowPlex platform that places decoys and tripwires in AI agent workflows and around AI infrastructure to detect agents that have been hijacked or are misbehaving. The company describes it as patent pending. SecurityBrief UK reported the launch the next day.

items.title: launch: Doppel Email Security becomes generally available
items.content_text: Doppel announced general availability of Email Security on 30 July 2026, in the Americas and Asia-Pacific regions, together with an AI managed service for its human risk management product. SecurityBrief UK reported the launch on 31 July 2026.

items.title: launch: Veeam Data Platform v13.1 becomes generally available
items.content_text: Veeam announced general availability of version 13.1, adding support for six more hypervisors, malware scanning of file shares, expanded threat detection for Azure, automated Active Directory forest recovery, and post-quantum and hybrid FIPS cryptography options. The release notes give 29 July 2026 as the download date.

items.title: launch: Anvilogic makes Blueprints generally available and adds search over cloud storage
items.content_text: Anvilogic announced general availability of Blueprints, with scheduling, customer-configured connectors, sharing across teams and daily AI budget controls, and a new federated search that reaches data left in Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage and Google Cloud Storage without moving it.

items.title: launch: Infoblox adds external attack surface management and supplier monitoring to Exposure Management
items.content_text: In a release dated 28 July 2026 Infoblox announced External Attack Surface Management and Supply Chain Intelligence as additions to Infoblox Exposure Management alongside Digital Risk Protection Services. The release mentions an early access programme and gives no general availability date.

items.title: launch: Intel 471 adds an AI agent and an MCP connector to Verity471
items.content_text: Intel 471 announced Agent471, an AI agent inside Verity471 that answers questions across a customer's subscribed intelligence with citations, and MCP471, a Model Context Protocol connector that brings the intelligence into AI tools the customer already runs. Help Net Security reported the announcement the same day.

items.title: launch: ZeroFox launches the HNTR platform and HNTR Executive Protection
items.content_text: ZeroFox announced on 28 July 2026 the general availability of HNTR, which it described as a new AI-first platform bringing its digital risk protection and threat intelligence together, and of HNTR Executive Protection as the first application on it. SiliconANGLE reported the launch the same day. The vendor's site now presents its solutions under the HNTR platform name.

items.title: launch: OneSpan introduces the DigipassONE authentication platform
items.content_text: OneSpan announced DigipassONE, a platform bringing together authentication, transaction signing, digital credentials, analytics and in-app protection, with DigipassONE Authenticate as the authentication module. The documentation states the platform software was formerly known as Digipass S3. In October 2026 OneSpan previewed a free passkey trial of DigipassONE Authenticate.

items.title: launch: Bolster AI adds fraudulent advert monitoring and takedowns to its platform
items.content_text: In a release dated 21 July 2026, Bolster AI announced detection of paid search and social adverts that impersonate a customer's brand, with takedown requests and monitoring for reappearance. The release said it was available at once as part of the platform; a knowledge-base article describes how the findings appear in the Web and Social Media modules.

items.title: certification: Black Kite announces GovRAMP status for its third-party risk intelligence product
items.content_text: Black Kite announced a GovRAMP status for its Third-Party Cyber Risk Intelligence product. The release's title says Ready while its body says Authorization; the GovRAMP participants list read on 2026-11-22 shows the product as Ready at Moderate.

items.title: acquisition: Cribl announces the acquisition of detection-coverage firm CardinalOps
items.content_text: Cribl announced on 14 July 2026 that it was acquiring CardinalOps, a company founded in 2020 whose platform measured an organisation's detection coverage against adversary behaviour and found and repaired broken or noisy detection rules in other vendors' SIEM and EDR tools. Terms were not disclosed. BankInfoSecurity reported that CardinalOps had 35 staff and had raised US$24 million; TechTarget reported Cribl's chief executive saying about 20 security engineers and the intellectual property would move to Cribl. Cribl said it would open a Tel Aviv office for the team. No separate statement that the transaction had closed was found; a Cribl release of 19 August 2026 refers to it as an acquisition made in July, and when checked for this record cardinalops.com redirected permanently to cribl.io. The technology was then built into Cribl Detect.

items.title: launch: Tidal Cyber announces threat-led asset visibility and vulnerability prioritisation
items.content_text: Tidal Cyber announced on 13 July 2026 two additions to its platform: a view of which assets matter to adversary procedures and where defences have blind spots, and ranking of vulnerabilities by their link to adversary procedures. The release did not say whether the platform discovers assets or scans for vulnerabilities itself or takes that data from other tools, and it gave no availability, edition or customer details.

items.title: acquisition: Aikido acquires Root, which patches open-source vulnerabilities in place
items.content_text: Aikido announced on 2026-06-30 that it had acquired Root (Root.io Inc., founded in 2020 as Slim.AI), whose AI agents build patches for open-source vulnerabilities at the versions customers already run. The capability is offered as Aikido Libraries and Aikido Images. Terms were not disclosed.

items.title: Dataset version 2026-11-22
items.content_text: 0 new vendors, 0 new products, 6 score changes, 0 vendor status changes, 126 events recorded.

items.title: launch: Redis Open Source 8.12 reaches general availability
items.content_text: The Redis GitHub release page, dated 22 November, describes 8.12.0 as the general availability release of Redis 8.12 in Redis Open Source. The notes list compressed bitmaps, a lower-memory encoding for large sorted sets, set member expiration, and an opt-in SQ8 compression option for HNSW vector indexes. The notes list no CVE fixes; availability in Redis Cloud or Redis Software was not checked.

items.title: security incident: Together AI discloses unauthorised download of stored customer prompt samples
items.content_text: According to a disclosure published by Together AI's chief executive on 2026-11-21, an unauthorised party downloaded samples of customer prompts that the company had stored in a private Hugging Face repository after a credential for that repository was committed to a public GitHub repository by an AI coding agent. The company says the samples came from serverless inference requests to three models, mainly on four days in June and July 2026, that the party searched them for credentials to other services, and that its review of whether personal or other customer data was exposed is continuing. Together AI does not state how many customers or requests were affected and says it is working with a forensic firm and law enforcement and has made zero data retention the default for new accounts.

items.title: launch: AWS Quick adds enterprise guardrails in preview
items.content_text: AWS announced on 2026-11-20 a preview of enterprise guardrails for AWS Quick, letting administrators apply content filters, denied topics, blocked words, prompt-attack detection and controls for selected personal data types to user prompts, by user, identity-provider group or account default, with a detect-only mode. AWS said the preview is open to select customers on the Professional and Enterprise plans.

items.title: certification: Dropzone AI says its AI SOC Analyst is FedRAMP High (Class D) certified through Second Front's platform
items.content_text: Dropzone AI said in a press release published on 2026-11-20 that its AI SOC Analyst had obtained FedRAMP High (Class D) certification through Second Front's 2F Game Warden platform, making it available to US federal agencies for production use. The release points to Second Front's FedRAMP Marketplace listing (FR2410866384) and names no authorising agency. That listing, checked on 2026-11-22, shows 2F Game Warden as FedRAMP Certified at Class D (High) since 2025-08-12 but does not name Dropzone AI, so the certification runs through Second Front's platform and Dropzone's inclusion rests on its own statement.

items.title: vulnerability disclosure: Palo Alto Networks advisory: critical Java flaw affects on-premises Idira components
items.content_text: According to a Palo Alto Networks security advisory dated 20 November 2026, a buffer overflow in the Java HotSpot JVM (CVE-2026-114938, rated critical by the vendor at CVSS-B 9.2) affects Idira Privilege Threat Analytics, the Idira Remote Access Connector and its CLI, and on-premises Idira Secure Access with an HTML5 Gateway, with fixed versions listed for each. The advisory says PAN-OS-based products are not affected, that SaaS products need no customer action, and that the company is not aware of malicious exploitation. It adds that review of the rest of the portfolio was continuing.

items.title: launch: Replit opens early access to Tunnels for reaching services on a private network
items.content_text: Replit announced Tunnels on 2026-11-20. A client run by the customer's IT team inside its network carries traffic between Replit workspaces and chosen internal services, such as databases and internal APIs, over a mutually authenticated TLS tunnel. Replit says this covers Agent tool calls and requests from published apps. It is early access only, by request, with no pricing given.

items.title: rebrand: Writer renames WRITER AI Studio to Control Center
items.content_text: Writer said on its blog on 2026-11-20 that WRITER AI Studio is now called Control Center, reflecting its role as the admin hub for agent governance after agent building moved into the main app. The navigation is reorganised into seven sections covering usage, activity logs, build governance, integrations, security, billing and settings. Writer said existing configurations and permissions are unchanged, and announced no pricing change.

items.title: funding: Anthropic lists on Nasdaq as ANT; IPO raises about US$93.5 billion gross
items.content_text: Anthropic announced on 2026-11-18 that it had priced its initial public offering at US$83.00 per Class A share, and its shares began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT on 2026-11-19. In a release dated 2026-11-20, Anthropic said the offering closed with 1,127,000,000 shares sold, including the underwriters' full option, for gross proceeds of about US$93.5 billion, of which about US$91.6 billion went to the company, and that a concurrent private placement to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, NVIDIA and TSMC Partners raised about US$26.0 billion more. Al Jazeera reported on 2026-11-19 that the shares first traded at US$111.50 and closed at US$97.17.

items.title: acquisition: Elastic signs agreement to acquire agent observability firm HoneyHive
items.content_text: Elastic said in a blog post dated 19 November 2026, and in its second-quarter fiscal 2027 results released the same day, that it has entered into an agreement to acquire HoneyHive, an AI agent observability and evaluation company. Elastic plans to bring HoneyHive's tracing and evaluation features into Elastic Observability. The deal had not closed at the time of the announcement and no terms were disclosed.

items.title: pricing change: Google Cloud makes Deferred tier generally available at 50% below Standard pay-as-you-go rates
items.content_text: Google Cloud's weekly news roundup, dated 19 November 2026, lists under the week of 16 to 20 November that the Deferred service tier is generally available on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform for the Interactions API, Agent Development Kit and Deep Research. The roundup and Google's documentation say deferred turns are billed at 50% below Standard pay-as-you-go rates; the documentation adds a 24-hour completion target with no credit-backed latency SLA and support on the global endpoint only. The exact launch day within that week is not stated.

items.title: certification: Horizon3 reports CMMC Final Level 2 (Self) status for its federal environment
items.content_text: Horizon3 announced in a press release dated 19 November 2026 that it has reached CMMC Final Level 2 (Self) status. The release describes a self-assessment against the 110 requirements of NIST SP 800-171 Revision 2, submitted and affirmed in the Supplier Performance Risk System, covering its federal product and sales environment; it names no third-party assessor. The release links the status to NodeZero for Government.

items.title: launch: LangChain puts LangSmith Tool Gateway into public beta
items.content_text: LangChain announced on 2026-11-19 a public beta of LangSmith Tool Gateway, a managed layer between agents and their tools that handles credentials, identity and access for each tool call and traces the calls in LangSmith. According to the post, deny policies and the audit log require contacting LangChain, and the audit log is an Enterprise plan feature.

items.title: certification: MongoDB says Atlas for Government has FedRAMP Class D (High) certification and now runs on Azure Government
items.content_text: MongoDB announced on 19 November 2026 that MongoDB Atlas for Government has achieved FedRAMP Class D certification, the class formerly called FedRAMP High, and that the service now supports Microsoft Azure Government alongside AWS and Google Cloud. The release says native vector search is available inside that environment. This is the company's own statement; the release does not give an authorization date or sponsoring agency, and the FedRAMP Marketplace listing was not checked.

items.title: regulatory action: California Attorney General serves investigative subpoena on NVIDIA
items.content_text: According to a press release from the California Attorney General's office dated 19 November 2026, Attorney General Rob Bonta served an investigative subpoena on NVIDIA. The office says it is examining, following press reports concerning the company's former chief executive, whether advanced chips or confidential information may have reached China and whether NVIDIA misled investors and the public. A subpoena is an investigative step; the release makes no finding that NVIDIA broke the law.

items.title: launch: Pinecone adds cost and usage export in the FOCUS billing format for Enterprise plans
items.content_text: A Pinecone blog post dated 2026-11-19 announced a Cost and Usage Export API that produces FOCUS v1.4 CSV files by project and index, covering any window in the past year. Pinecone says it is available to organisations on the Enterprise plan, from the console or the Admin API.

items.title: partnership: Salesforce says US Commerce Department selected its consortium for a technology export programme
items.content_text: Salesforce announced on 2026-11-19 that the US Department of Commerce had selected a consortium it leads as one of 33 initial consortia in the American SI Exports Program, which Salesforce says brings priority government promotion to foreign buyers and priority export-control review. Agentforce is one component of the package, alongside Hyperforce, Data 360, Informatica and the Einstein Trust Layer. Other consortium members are not named, and no Commerce Department notice was read.

items.title: partnership: SentinelOne partners with Singapore's Digital and Intelligence Service on cyber defence
items.content_text: A SentinelOne press release dated 2026-11-19, distributed by Business Wire and read on Finviz, announced a partnership with the Defence Cyber Command of Singapore's Digital and Intelligence Service. The release says the two will explore cooperation on cybersecurity technology, threat intelligence sharing, research and training for Singapore's defence and critical infrastructure sectors.

items.title: pricing change: Sourcegraph lowers credit costs for Deep Search and Code Finder and changes service-account billing
items.content_text: Sourcegraph announced on 2026-11-19 that a Deep Search now costs 50 credits instead of 70, a Code Finder call through MCP costs 3 credits instead of 11, and Smart Hovers no longer use credits, effective the same day for all customers. The post also says service accounts used for searches and other product workflows are billed on the same model as human users from that date.

items.title: partnership: Teleport gains AWS Security Competency status for identity and access management
items.content_text: Teleport announced on 2026-11-19 that it has earned AWS Security Competency status in the Identity and Access Management category, an Amazon Web Services partner designation. This is a partner-programme recognition announced by the vendor, not an independent security certification.

items.title: launch: Together AI launches Storage Accelerator caching for its GPU clusters
items.content_text: Together AI announced on 2026-11-19 the Together Storage Accelerator, a caching layer that keeps data read from S3-compatible storage and Hugging Face Hub on a GPU cluster's local NVMe drives so later reads are served inside the cluster. The company's post says it is available now and included at no extra cost with every Together GPU Cluster; the speed figures quoted are from Together's own tests.

items.title: launch: Yubico unveils YubiID identity platform in early access and a post-quantum-ready YubiKey in public beta
items.content_text: In a release for its Capital Markets Day on 2026-11-19, Yubico said YubiID, a digital identity platform extending the company into software and lifecycle services, is in limited early access with design partners, and that a next-generation, post-quantum-ready YubiKey is in public beta. It restated the financial targets adopted on 2026-11-05: average annual net sales growth of 15-20% over five years and an EBIT margin moving toward 20% by 2031.

items.title: partnership: Akamai and Microsoft bring Akamai Workforce Protector to Edge for Business on mobile
items.content_text: Akamai announced on 2026-11-18 a collaboration with Microsoft under which organisations can deploy the Akamai Workforce Protector extension (formerly LayerX) in Microsoft Edge for Business on managed iOS and Android devices, using Microsoft's deployment tools. The release does not concern Akamai Guardicore Segmentation.

items.title: partnership: Check Point expands Microsoft collaboration to run its SASE platform on Azure
items.content_text: Check Point announced on 2026-11-18 an expanded collaboration with Microsoft to deploy Check Point SASE on Microsoft Azure, citing 48 additional Azure points of presence and integration with Microsoft Entra. Check Point said it expects the service to be available through Microsoft Marketplace in the first half of 2027.

items.title: launch: Delinea releases a Microsoft Sentinel solution for Delinea Platform privileged access events
items.content_text: Delinea announced on 18 November 2026 a Microsoft Sentinel solution that sends Delinea Platform audit events, including secret access, authentication, session activity and configuration changes, into Sentinel with analytic rules, hunting queries and workbooks. The company says it is available in the Microsoft Marketplace and the Sentinel Content Hub.

items.title: launch: Elastic makes Jina embeddings v5 text and omni models available in Microsoft Foundry
items.content_text: Elastic announced in a press release dated 18 November 2026 that its Jina embeddings v5 text and omni models are in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog, where customers can deploy them as dedicated endpoints in their own Azure environments. The release says the omni models cover image, audio and video in one vector space.

items.title: launch: Keeper launches an emergency breach response service built around KeeperPAM
items.content_text: Keeper Security announced on 2026-11-18 a global emergency service for organisations under active attack. According to the company, requests go through an emergency portal to its solution engineering team, which helps deploy KeeperPAM to revoke standing privileges and rotate compromised credentials. Keeper does not publish pricing and says commercial terms are discussed after containment.

items.title: launch: OneTrust announces Fall '26 Release with AI model intelligence, lineage views and AI-run third-party research
items.content_text: OneTrust announced its Fall '26 Release on 18 November 2026. For AI Governance it adds a curated library of third-party foundation-model information in the AI inventory, an interactive lineage view across systems, models, agents and controls, and usage and risk dashboards. For Third-Party Management it lets a workflow rule trigger an AI research skill that gathers public information and drafts questionnaire answers, and widens AI document scanning. The release gives no availability date or packaging details.

items.title: acquisition: Palo Alto Networks agrees to acquire Applied Compute in an all-stock deal valued at US$4.5 billion
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks announced on 18 November 2026 a definitive agreement to acquire Applied Compute, which provides a platform for post-training and running open-weight AI models. The company's release values the all-stock deal at US$4.5 billion, subject to adjustments, and expects it to close in its fiscal third quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory clearance. It does not name which existing product lines will change; the deal had not closed when this was recorded.

items.title: partnership: Cognizant joins the Qualys managed risk operations centre (mROC) alliance
items.content_text: Qualys announced on 2026-11-18 that Cognizant had joined its Global mROC Alliance and will offer four managed services built on Qualys Enterprise TruRisk Management: risk quantification and advisory, onboarding and integration, managed risk monitoring, and managed remediation. The release describes the service as using Qualys InstaScan, Agent Val and TruRisk Eliminate. Performance figures in the release are Qualys's own.

items.title: partnership: Reflection AI describes Gray Swan red-teaming of its Beam model
items.content_text: Reflection AI published on 2026-11-18 an account of its work with Gray Swan, whose automated red-teaming system tested Beam in cyber, biology, chemistry, influence-operation and general harmful-content scenarios, and whose prompt-injection challenge was used for agent testing. Reflection says Gray Swan data was added to Beam's safety training. The post reports its own results, including that Beam chose an insecure fix that passed tests in 6 of 44 episodes; Gray Swan's own account was not read.

items.title: partnership: Replit announces general availability of Microsoft Fabric and Teams integrations
items.content_text: In a post dated 2026-11-18, Replit said its Microsoft Fabric integration is generally available after a June preview, that its Teams integration is becoming generally available, and that publishing apps into a customer's Azure tenant is in early access through Microsoft Marketplace. It also said local work in its desktop app is generally available. Running Replit fully inside a customer's Azure environment was described as a future step.

items.title: launch: Sumo Logic releases AWS Observability Solution v3.0.0 with 20 regions and Marketplace deployment
items.content_text: Sumo Logic announced on 2026-11-18 an expanded AWS Observability Solution that adds the Zurich, Melbourne and New Zealand regions, for 20 supported AWS regions, and can be bought and deployed through AWS Marketplace Quick Launch. The press release says version 3.0.0 is available to Sumo Logic customers now. The release concerns observability rather than the Cloud SIEM product.

items.title: launch: Sysdig makes its MCP server for Sysdig Monitor generally available
items.content_text: Sysdig announced on 2026-11-18 that its MCP server for monitoring is generally available, connecting AI assistants to live Kubernetes, container and cloud monitoring data in Sysdig Monitor under the same team permissions as the product's interface. The post concerns Sysdig Monitor rather than Sysdig Secure.

items.title: launch: Zafran announces Offensive Validation, AI-agent attack testing for its exposure platform
items.content_text: Zafran announced Offensive Validation on its website on 2026-11-18 as a new part of its exposure management platform. Zafran says AI agents test internal and internet-facing assets to show which exposures are actually exploitable, check whether mitigations and fixes hold, and run inside isolated sandboxes under customer-set rules of engagement. The post does not state whether the feature is generally available or give pricing.

items.title: launch: Cato Networks announces AgentSense runtime guardrail for AI agents
items.content_text: Cato Networks announced on 2026-11-17, in a release distributed by PR Newswire, a capability called AgentSense that assesses AI agents while they run and aims to block unsafe actions, including those steered by untrusted content. Cato said it is integrated in the Cato platform and included at no extra charge in Cato AI Usage licences; a drift detection function was described as still to come.

items.title: launch: Cerebras puts disaggregated inference into production, pairing GPUs with its CS-3 systems
items.content_text: Cerebras announced on its blog on 2026-11-17 that it is running disaggregated inference in production, with AMD Instinct GPUs handling prompt processing and its CS-3 systems generating responses. Cerebras said it measured five times the throughput per megawatt of a CS-3-only setup, is using the approach on its Inference Cloud, and has given early access to partners including Amazon Web Services and Fireworks AI.

items.title: launch: Cogent introduces DefenseOS with Agent Policies and Agent Automations
items.content_text: Cogent announced on its blog on 2026-11-17 DefenseOS, which it describes as the context engine and agent harness at the core of its platform, together with Agent Policies for encoding an organisation's rules and Agent Automations for scheduled or event-triggered security work. The post does not give pricing or a general availability date.

items.title: launch: Cognition introduces Devin Bots, persistent agents that manage teams of Devin agents
items.content_text: Fortune reported on 17 November 2026 that Cognition launched Devin Bots, persistent agents that split up work, assign it to Devin agents and keep context over projects lasting days or weeks. According to the article, dozens of customers have early access; it does not state general availability or pricing.

items.title: launch: Cohere adds a Crunchbase connector to North
items.content_text: Cohere said in a blog post dated 17 November 2026 that North now has a Crunchbase connector giving access to private-company data such as funding and acquisition history. According to the post, it is available to North customers who hold their own Crunchbase licence and have single sign-on enabled, and figures drawn from Crunchbase carry citations.

items.title: partnership: DataRobot and Dell Technologies offer on-premises agentic AI blueprint for Middle East enterprises
items.content_text: DataRobot said in a press release dated 17 November 2026 that it is working with Dell Technologies to combine the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA and the DataRobot Agent Workforce Platform for Middle East customers running on-premises, private or hybrid environments. The release says a DataRobot blueprint is offered through the Dell Automation Platform, with financial services and logistics as initial focus sectors.

items.title: launch: GitHub Copilot app adds GA support for GitHub Enterprise Server; browser use enters preview
items.content_text: GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says the GitHub Copilot app's support for GitHub Enterprise Server accounts is now generally available, and that Azure DevOps repository support and browser use, in which Copilot operates a Chromium-based browser in an isolated tab group, are in public preview. The entry says browser use is off by default and states no plan or pricing changes.

items.title: launch: GitHub puts on-demand secret scanning in Copilot's security review into public preview
items.content_text: GitHub's changelog of 17 November 2026 says Copilot's security review now runs GitHub's secret scanning detectors on code changes before merge, in public preview, across Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, Copilot SDK integrations and Copilot code review. The entry says the feature is off by default, is not yet in VS Code, and that scans consume AI credits under the Secret Protection AI Credit SKU.

items.title: launch: H2O.ai makes TimeH2O and TabH2O foundation models generally available on H2O AI Cloud
items.content_text: H2O.ai announced in a press release dated 17 November 2026 that TimeH2O, a time-series foundation model, and TabH2O, a tabular foundation model, are generally available on H2O AI Cloud for production use and fine-tuning. The release says TimeH2O-v1 open weights are published for research under a non-commercial licence, with production use needing a licence from H2O.ai. The benchmark rankings it cites are reported by H2O.ai itself.

items.title: launch: Incode launches Know Your Agent, tying AI agents to a verified person
items.content_text: Incode announced on 2026-11-17 a product called Incode Know Your Agent. According to the company's release, it detects AI agents in a business's traffic, checks the person behind an agent with a live face match against a government record, lets that person set limits on what the agent may do, and logs agent actions against those limits. Incode says it is available now; the release names no customers or partners.

items.title: launch: LangSmith adds access controls for trace inputs and outputs on Enterprise plans
items.content_text: LangChain announced on 2026-11-17 three access controls for LangSmith: restricting who can see trace inputs and outputs, user groups with per-workspace permissions, and policies that decide trace visibility from run metadata such as a customer ID. The company says the controls are available on LangSmith Enterprise plans and that traces are still stored in full.

items.title: security incident: Malicious versions of Microsoft's agent-framework Python package published on PyPI
items.content_text: Reported by The Hacker News and BleepingComputer on 2026-11-18: attackers published two malicious versions (1.26.1 and 1.26.2) of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI on 2026-11-17. Both outlets say the versions carried a credential stealer that ran whenever Python started and targeted cloud and CI credentials, that PyPI quarantined them, and that it is not known how the attacker obtained publishing access. The Hacker News, in an update dated 2026-11-20, quotes a Microsoft spokesperson saying the company made some repositories private while it investigates.

items.title: launch: Microsoft's Ignite 2026 keynote: unified Copilot experience, more models for Foundry, Cobalt 200 VMs generally available
items.content_text: Microsoft published an edited version of Satya Nadella's Ignite keynote on 2026-11-17. It describes a unified Copilot experience spanning Chat, Cowork, Code and Autopilot, says GPT 6.2 and Meta's latest models are coming to Foundry, and says Cobalt 200 virtual machines are generally available. Microsoft also claims its Maia 300 chip delivers 40% more tokens per watt than leading GPU-based systems. The post gives no prices and, for most items, no availability dates.

items.title: launch: Microsoft makes Perception security agents generally available and folds Sentinel SIEM features into Defender
items.content_text: In a Microsoft Security blog post dated 2026-11-17, Microsoft said Perception, a system that coordinates attack-simulation, detection and remediation agents, is generally available. It also said the core of an Integrated Security Operations Center in Defender is generally available, giving eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 customers Sentinel SIEM features and 90-day default retention for Defender data. Entra dynamic permissions and Conditional Access controls are in limited preview, and several Purview data-protection features for Copilot are due in preview or general availability in January 2027. No prices are listed.

items.title: corporate restructuring: NVIDIA board creates a standing National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee
items.content_text: NVIDIA announced on 17 November 2026 that its board has set up a standing committee to oversee national security policy, export control compliance and global trade risk. It is chaired by Suzanne Nora Johnson, with Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members; the company's national security and trade compliance teams will report to the committee and to interim chief executive Colette Kress. The release does not link the committee to any named investigation or proceeding.

items.title: launch: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol in ChatGPT, Codex and the API
items.content_text: OpenAI announced GPT-6.2 Astra, its new frontier model, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a more efficient everyday model; OpenAI's news feed dates the post 17 November 2026. The post says both are available to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex and to developers through the API, with Astra priced at US$8 per million input tokens and US$40 per million output tokens, 20% below GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI also states that GPT-6.2 Astra is its first externally released model to meet its own High threshold for AI self-improvement.

items.title: launch: Perforce announces general availability of parallel Python debugging in TotalView
items.content_text: A Perforce press release dated 2026-11-17 announced that parallel Python debugging is generally available in its TotalView debugger. The announcement concerns TotalView and not the Delphix data products.

items.title: launch: Pinecone releases one-job conversion of legacy vector indexes to document indexes
items.content_text: A Pinecone blog post dated 2026-11-17 announced a job that converts a legacy serverless vector index into a document index without re-embedding, while the old index keeps serving traffic. Pinecone says it applies to the Standard and Enterprise plans and is billed at the bulk import rate of US$0.25 per GB. Customers must then move search and write calls to the Documents API.

items.title: launch: Reflection AI opens a Trusted Access Program, starting with a penetration-testing tool
items.content_text: Reflection AI announced on 2026-11-17 a Trusted Access Program that gives vetted organisations early access to selected capabilities for defensive security work. The first offering is Laser, an autonomous penetration-testing harness built for its Mirror terminal agent, offered as a research preview to accepted commercial partners only.

items.title: launch: Replit introduces Missions, in which groups of agents work toward a stated outcome within a budget
items.content_text: Replit announced Missions on 2026-11-17. A user states an outcome, success criteria, a budget and approval rules; several agents then work in parallel and a separate AI judge checks results against the criteria, with work stopping if the budget runs out. The post gives no plan tiers or list prices, and its benchmark figures are Replit's own.

items.title: launch: Sweet Security adds Reachability mapping of internet routes to cloud workloads
items.content_text: Sweet Security announced on 2026-11-17 a Reachability feature that maps how the internet reaches, or is configured to reach, each workload, distinguishing routes seen in runtime traffic from routes that configuration allows. The company's post says the feature is available to all Sweet customers.

items.title: launch: Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max flagship model
items.content_text: Alibaba announced Qwen4-Max on 2026-11-16, describing it as the most capable Qwen model so far, with native vision and a one-million-token context window, available through QwenCloud's Token Plan and API. A follow-up Alibaba Cloud post on 2026-11-17 presented the model to enterprise teams. Neither post named Model Studio as a launch channel, and Alibaba said smaller open-weight Qwen4 models would follow without giving a date.

items.title: launch: Exaforce introduces ExaU for building custom security AI agents
items.content_text: Exaforce said in a blog post dated 16 November 2026 that ExaU lets security teams create their own AI agents, which it calls Exabots, with defined roles, persistent memory, scheduled routines and permission boundaries. The post says actions that change data need the user's approval and that ExaU is included in the Exaforce platform and available now; it gives no pricing.

items.title: partnership: Fiddler AI and AMD describe joint approach to running monitored AI agents on AMD hardware
items.content_text: A post on Fiddler AI's blog dated 16 November 2026, which says it first appeared on AMD's blog, describes a technical collaboration in which AMD supplies accelerated computing and open software and Fiddler supplies evaluation, observability and guardrails for agents running on it. The post mentions no investment or commercial terms.

items.title: outage: GitHub reports roughly six-hour degradation of pull requests, Actions and Git operations
items.content_text: According to GitHub's status page, an incident on 16 November 2026 degraded pull requests, GitHub Actions and Git push and fetch latency, with impact from about 09:30 to 15:55 UTC. GitHub's post-incident summary attributes it to storage servers holding Git repository data reaching disk read bandwidth limits during a planned repository migration, made worse by a disk configuration setting, and says the same cause produced a shorter event on 13 November.

items.title: launch: LangChain reorganises LangSmith around a per-agent record and announces the LangSmith Agent Platform
items.content_text: LangChain announced on 2026-11-16 that LangSmith has been rebuilt around an agent record: each agent gets an owner, an immutable ID and a type, with environments and traces grouped under it. The company says agents on any OpenTelemetry-compatible platform can be registered alongside those built in LangSmith, and that the new version is available in cloud, bring-your-own-cloud and self-hosted deployments. No pricing change is mentioned.

items.title: Dataset version 2026-11-20
items.content_text: 240 new vendors, 314 new products, 0 score changes, 0 vendor status changes, 1002 events recorded.

items.title: partnership: Reality Defender says Microsoft named it a synthetic media detection partner for Teams
items.content_text: Reality Defender stated on 2026-11-20 that Microsoft, at its Ignite conference that week, named it one of four synthetic media detection partners for Microsoft Teams, with RealMeeting showing results to the meeting organiser inside Teams. This is the vendor's account; a Microsoft source naming the partners was not found.

items.title: launch: MIND adds email data loss prevention for Microsoft Exchange
items.content_text: MIND announced an email module that classifies message and attachment content against the recipient and can block outbound Microsoft Exchange mail before delivery, using the same policies as its other channels.

items.title: launch: Saviynt launches EU identity security offering on S3NS trusted cloud
items.content_text: Saviynt announced an EU offering delivered as SaaS on S3NS's SecNumCloud-qualified cloud, separated from its global commercial cloud and operated by EU residents, with Thales as operations partner.

items.title: acquisition: Novacoast acquires UpGuard's managed vendor assessment business
items.content_text: UpGuard announced that Novacoast acquired its managed vendor assessments service business, with the delivering analysts moving to Novacoast from 2026-11-15. Customers continue to use the UpGuard platform. Terms were not disclosed.

items.title: litigation: Federal dockets show at least ten new suits naming X.AI Corp. since mid-September 2026
items.content_text: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): the ten most recent of 58 dockets naming X.AI were all filed between 2026-09-17 and 2026-11-19. They include several Doe v. X.AI Corp. cases in W.D. Ark., NAACP v. X.AI in the Fifth Circuit, Carter v. X.AI Corp. in W.D. Tenn., Mueller v. X.AI Corp. in N.D. Ill., Saylor v. X.AI Corp. in C.D. Cal. and Al-Khatahtbeh v. X.AI Corp. in N.D. Cal. The claims were not reviewed.

items.title: launch: BioCatch announces New Zealand banks will launch an intelligence-sharing network
items.content_text: BioCatch's news index lists a release dated 2026-11-18 stating that New Zealand banks are to launch an intelligence-sharing network to combat fraud and scams. A release the same day reported results from BioCatch Trust Australia, which launched in November 2024 with five banks.

items.title: leadership change: H2O.ai appoints a chief financial officer
items.content_text: H2O.ai announced the appointment of Steven Vattuone, previously chief financial officer of ON24, as its chief financial officer.

items.title: launch: Holistic AI releases Agentic Red Teaming 2.0
items.content_text: A platform update adds agent profiling, adaptive attacks and tests for data extraction, tool abuse, bias and sycophancy, with evidence, severity and a recommended fix for each finding.

items.title: certification: Horizon3 announces Impact Level 4 authorisation for NodeZero for Defense
items.content_text: Horizon3 announced that NodeZero for Defense, covering internal pentesting with risk-based exposure management, is included in an Impact Level 4 authorisation and is available to US defence customers. The release does not name the authorising body.

items.title: launch: MIND makes Microsoft 365 and Copilot integrations generally available
items.content_text: MIND announced generally available integrations with Microsoft Copilot, Purview, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Edge and Exchange, including reading and applying Purview sensitivity labels and a Windows endpoint agent, and said the product can be bought through the Microsoft Marketplace.

items.title: partnership: NICE announces NiCE Cognigy integrations with Microsoft Teams, Azure and Dynamics 365
items.content_text: NICE announced that NiCE Cognigy had completed certification as a voice agent for Microsoft Teams Phone, able to answer calls and transfer callers with context, and a new integration with Azure, Teams and Dynamics 365 Customer Service. The offerings were stated to be available on Microsoft Marketplace.

items.title: launch: Pentera Apps announced for web application and API testing
items.content_text: Pentera announced Pentera Apps, agent-based testing of web applications and APIs, in early availability after a beta with more than 60 customers. A July 2026 release had put general availability in the fourth quarter of 2026.

items.title: launch: Pindrop launches Pindrop for Hiring; Pulse for Meetings certified for Microsoft Teams
items.content_text: Pindrop announced on 2026-11-18 a new product, Pindrop for Hiring, and said its Pulse for Meetings integration had earned Microsoft Teams certification, with in-meeting warnings and detection events that can flow into Microsoft Defender workflows.

items.title: partnership: Tonic.ai approved to de-identify Spirit Airlines dataset being sold to Google
items.content_text: Tonic.ai announced that the US Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York approved its contract to act as independent third party de-identifying a corporate dataset that Google is buying from Spirit Airlines in bankruptcy proceedings.

items.title: partnership: Ent joins Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program and lists on Microsoft Marketplace
items.content_text: Ent said it had joined the Microsoft for Startups Pegasus Program, was available on Microsoft Marketplace, and had integrations with Microsoft Defender XDR, Sentinel, Purview, Entra ID, Intune and Security Copilot.

items.title: litigation: Two civil suits filed against Fireworks AI in the Northern District of California
items.content_text: According to the CourtListener federal docket index, searched on 2026-11-20, Komorski v. Fireworks AI, Inc. (3:26-cv-13987) was filed on 17 November 2026 and Brethelette v. Fireworks.AI, Inc. (3:26-cv-14080) on 18 November 2026, both in the Northern District of California. The complaints were not retrieved, so what the suits allege is not established.

items.title: launch: Genesys launches Standalone AI Agents and Genesys Arena
items.content_text: Genesys announced Standalone AI Agents, which let an organisation deploy the Genesys Cloud Agentic Virtual Agent without moving its contact centre to Genesys Cloud, together with Genesys Arena, a set of prebuilt agent kits, and an effort-based pricing model.

items.title: launch: Microsoft AI announces MAI Code 2, MAI Image 2.7, MAI Cyber 2 Flash and other models at Ignite
items.content_text: Microsoft AI announced on 2026-11-17 a set of new in-house models: MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, MAI Image 2.7 and 2.7 Flash, MAI Cyber 2 Flash, MAI Realtime 1, a transcription model built on MAI Transcribe 2 and Decision 1.1. It also described MAI Licensed Weights, under which a customer customises an MAI model with its own data and runs it in its own Azure environment, initially through Microsoft's own engagement teams. Availability differs by model; MAI Code 2 Flash was described as a limited-access preview in Foundry.

items.title: certification: LS2 HSM module validated to FIPS 140-3 Level 3 with ML-KEM and ML-DSA
items.content_text: The NIST register shows certificate #5588 for the LS2 HSM Family module, validated on 2026-11-16 at FIPS 140-3 overall Level 3, with the post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA among its approved algorithms. The certificate runs to 2031-11-15.

items.title: litigation: Anaconda files copyright case naming Alibaba Group and Alibaba Cloud in Delaware federal court
items.content_text: According to the federal docket index published by CourtListener, Anaconda, Inc. filed a copyright case against Alibaba Group Holding Limited in the US District Court for the District of Delaware on 2026-11-13 (No. 1:26-cv-01466), with Alibaba Cloud listed among the parties. The claims and any response were not reviewed.

items.title: funding: LangChain announces US$300 million Series C at US$3 billion valuation
items.content_text: LangChain announced on 2026-11-13 a US$300 million Series C at a US$3 billion valuation led by existing investor CapitalG, with new investors including GIC and DFJ Growth. It said more than 7,000 organisations use LangSmith.

items.title: launch: NICE launches a next generation of NiCE Cognigy with reusable skills and decision tracing
items.content_text: NICE announced a new generation of NiCE Cognigy with a redesigned builder, agents assembled from reusable skills, tools and personas, an AI assistant for building and testing, tracing of each step an agent takes, and native speech-to-speech models. Existing deployments continue unchanged; default models are included in the conversation price and premium third-party models are billed on usage.

items.title: outage: Worldwide Microsoft 365 outage lasts nearly 24 hours; Copilot among services affected
items.content_text: Reported by BleepingComputer on 2026-11-16 and by ITPro: an outage that began on 12 November 2026 disrupted Microsoft 365 services worldwide for nearly 24 hours, including Outlook, Exchange Online, Teams and Copilot. Both reported Microsoft's preliminary account that a latent software defect, extra load after a Teams failover and reduced server capacity caused a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive. A final post-incident report had not been published when this was recorded.

items.title: leadership change: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.content_text: NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect, without stating a reason. Colette Kress became interim chief executive while remaining chief financial officer, and Harvey C. Jones was appointed board chair.

items.title: launch: Picus Security launches agentic Autonomous Penetration Testing with scope approval and a kill switch
items.content_text: Picus Security announced on 12 November 2026 that Picus Autonomous Penetration Testing was available to customers as part of its platform, with the fully agentic mode in early access. The company described business approval of scope and techniques before a run, hard-deny rules against destructive actions, a kill switch, three autonomy levels and logging of every action. No customer was named.

items.title: certification: Polaris listed on FedRAMP Marketplace as in process; not yet authorised
items.content_text: Black Duck announced that the Polaris Platform is listed on the FedRAMP Marketplace in the initial implementation phase and that it is pursuing FedRAMP 20x Class C certification with an assessment against the Rev5 Moderate baseline. The product is not yet authorised.

items.title: partnership: Rafay and Fortanix announce joint confidential AI as a service offering
items.content_text: Rafay Systems and Fortanix announced that the Rafay platform orchestrates workloads on CNCF Confidential Containers using Fortanix Confidential AI. In the joint design Data Security Manager releases encryption keys only to environments attested by Fortanix Confidential Computing Manager.

items.title: launch: Varonis adds LLM Gateway and MCP Gateway to Atlas AI Security
items.content_text: The Varonis changelog records the release of an LLM Gateway for controlling AI model usage and spend and an MCP Gateway for governing agent tool access, both within Atlas AI Security, followed on 12 November by an Agent Manifest feature.

items.title: acquisition: Cogent agrees to acquire Specular
items.content_text: Pulse 2.0 reported on 2026-11-11 that Cogent had announced an agreement to acquire Specular, a company whose AI agents probe an organisation from the internet to find exposed assets and test how they could be exploited. Terms were not disclosed. Specular's founder is to lead offensive security at Cogent, and the external testing is to be combined with Cogent's remediation tools. Cogent's newsroom dates the announcement 2026-11-10.

items.title: launch: Cyera announces Cy Agents and Cyera Endpoint
items.content_text: At its datasecAI 2026 event Cyera announced Cy Agents, a set of AI agents for detection, triage and investigation, and Cyera Endpoint, an on-device sensor that extends data loss prevention to laptops and workstations. The release does not say whether either is generally available.

items.title: leadership change: Feedzai appoints Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer
items.content_text: Feedzai's press-release index lists a release dated 2026-11-10 announcing Joost van Mook as chief revenue officer; the leadership page shows him in that role.

items.title: partnership: Illumio joins World Wide Technology's ARMOR framework for AI risk
items.content_text: Illumio announced on 2026-11-10 that it will be featured in World Wide Technology's AI Readiness Model for Operational Resilience (ARMOR), naming Illumio Insights and Illumio Segmentation.

items.title: launch: One Identity releases Safeguard 9.0
items.content_text: One Identity announced Safeguard 9.0 on 2026-11-10, comprising Safeguard for Privileged Passwords 9.0 and Safeguard for Privileged Sessions 9.0. The release moves to hardware-agnostic deployment, adds just-in-time group elevation scoped to an asset, ESXi account discovery and TLS 1.3 support.

items.title: launch: Orca adds discovery of shadow AI applications and AI agents to its platform
items.content_text: Orca announced platform additions that detect applications built with AI app builders, inventory cloud-managed and self-hosted AI agents with their models, tools, identities and reachable data, and attribute code to the agents that produced it.

items.title: certification: Phio TX receives EUCC certificate at assurance level substantial
items.content_text: ENISA's register shows an EUCC certificate (EUCC-3095-2026-000003-I-00) issued on 2026-11-10 by DEKRA Testing and Certification for Quantum Xchange's PhioTX-V version 4.5.6 at assurance level substantial (EAL2), valid to 2031-11-09. The company announced it on 2026-11-12.

items.title: partnership: Cisco says it will add Anthropic's Claude Mythos to AI Defense adaptive red teaming
items.content_text: In a release dated 2026-11-09 Cisco said it is adding Anthropic's Claude Mythos model to the adaptive red-teaming framework in AI Defense, restricted to registered targets and authenticated operators, and described it as coming soon for select enterprises. The same release said AI Defense has been used by hundreds of customers since its January 2025 launch; no customers were named.

items.title: security incident: Fireworks AI discloses a second intrusion that reached account and billing information
items.content_text: Fireworks AI disclosed in bulletins of 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17 a second, separate incident between 23 and 30 October 2026. It said an intruder entered through development machines at a third-party cloud provider that had itself been breached and reached part of production, accessing account and billing information for all accounts created before 30 October and datasets, models or secrets for a small number of customers. It said it does not store card numbers and that the investigation was still open. UiPath, which uses Fireworks AI as a sub-processor, said on its trust centre that it found no indication its customers' data was affected and rotated keys as a precaution.

items.title: security incident: Teleport discloses exposure of internal chat transcripts through sub-processor Notion
items.content_text: Disclosed by Teleport on 2026-11-11: its sub-processor Notion told it on 9 November 2026 of a data breach affecting Teleport's chat transcripts in the Notion AI app. Teleport said the breach did not occur through its own systems or involve its products, that the transcripts contained links to internal pages and one office guest Wi-Fi password, which it rotated, and no credentials or specific customer data. It notified customers mentioned in the transcripts on 10 November, disabled Notion's AI features and rated the risk to customers as low.

items.title: litigation: Federal dockets show patent and copyright suits filed against Sophos in 2025-2026
items.content_text: According to federal dockets indexed by CourtListener (searched 2026-11-20): suits filed against Sophos entities include Long Horizon Technologies LLC v. Sophos Limited (E.D. Tex., filed 2026-11-08), Arc Link LLC v. Sophos Limited (patent, E.D. Tex., filed 2026-06-18), Fast Corporation Ltd. v. Sophos Ltd. (copyright, S.D.N.Y., filed 2026-03-25) and Sulaco Enterprises LLC v. Sophos Limited (patent, E.D. Tex., filed 2025-12-16). The claims were not reviewed.

items.title: leadership change: Checkmarx appoints Kobi Sivilya as chief information security officer
items.content_text: Checkmarx announced on 2026-11-05 the appointment of Kobi Sivilya to oversee security, IT and business applications. The release quotes chief executive Sandeep Johri.

items.title: launch: Cyberhaven puts Agentic Data Security module on sale
items.content_text: Cyberhaven announced that Agentic Data Security, a Flow module that finds AI agents, records their prompts, tool calls and file reads, and applies data policies to their actions, was available for purchase.

items.title: certification: CryptoHub receives Veeam Ready Security qualification for key management
items.content_text: Futurex announced that CryptoHub was qualified under Veeam's key management system compatibility category for Veeam Backup & Replication, integrating through KMIP.

items.title: acquisition: Sierra acquires browser-agent infrastructure company Anon
items.content_text: Sierra announced that Anon, which built infrastructure for AI agents to sign in to and operate websites that have no API, is joining Sierra. Terms were not disclosed. Sierra said the technology will let its agents work in systems without APIs.

items.title: partnership: Sumsub and Jelou announce an identity verification partnership
items.content_text: Sumsub's newsroom lists a 5 November 2026 announcement of a partnership with Jelou to connect identity verification with financial-services journeys started in WhatsApp.

items.title: launch: Veriff introduces Presence Verification for deepfake and coercion detection
items.content_text: Veriff announced Presence Verification, which it describes as combining deepfake and injection detection, coercion detection and device and network signals into one automated decision.

items.title: layoff: NICE says it will cut about 5% of its global workforce
items.content_text: Announced by NICE in its third-quarter 2026 results on 2026-11-04: it expects to reduce its global workforce by approximately 5%, with pre-tax restructuring charges of roughly $15 to $20 million, mostly in the fourth quarter. Reported by The Jerusalem Post and HR Katha on the same day as about 500 of roughly 10,000 employees, linked to the effect of AI on the customer-service software market.

items.title: funding: Sentra raises US$150M led by Capital One Ventures
